governed_construct: A DTO type declared in the unit: a class, interface or type alias whose name ends in 'Dto' or 'DTO'. Each such declaration is one instance; its conformance covers both its declaration and every value of that type in the unit.
interpretation: The rule asks that DTOs be immutable once created. A DTO declaration conforms when every property is readonly (readonly modifier, readonly constructor parameter property, or wrapping in Readonly<...>), and no value of that DTO type is modified anywhere in the unit after creation. Modification means a property assignment, compound assignment, ++/--, delete, Object.assign targeting the value, a write through an alias that was assigned the DTO value (for example a widened mutable type), a mutating method on a DTO field (push, splice, sort and similar on an array field), or a non-constructor method that writes this.<field>. Constructor initialisation of fields does not count as modification. Creating a new object (spread, factory, with-style method) does not count either. Object.freeze is allowed but not required. Which values are DTOs is decided by static type (inferred return types, Map.get results, parameter annotations), not by variable name, which is why the rule is T3. A unit with no DTO-named type is NOT_APPLICABLE, even if it mutates other objects.
